name: agent-fs-per-path-permission
body:
Law (prose; assessed by review): the per-path permission scoping IS the mechanism. A custom suite tool's path argument is matched against the acting agent's granted path globs in its permission block (the same glob mechanism as `edit`, worktree-mirrored), so the grant is scoped to exactly the role's owned surface rather than the tool being allowed wholesale.

Acceptance: a generated implementer's permission block expresses `apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp` as a deny-by-default glob map whose allow entries are exactly the role's owned path globs plus their `apg/.worktrees/*/` mirrors — never a scalar `: allow`, and never a blanket `"*": allow`. A path outside the granted globs is refused by the permission layer.

FALLBACK (open question, to confirm against opencode): if opencode treats a custom tool's permission as tool-level only (no per-path argument matching), the scoping must instead be enforced inside the tool — it resolves its path argument against the caller's project directory and refuses a path outside the acting role's granted surface. The requirement's observable acceptance (out-of-scope path refused) is unchanged under either mechanism; only where the enforcement lives moves.
